items.stem: Which object is the star at the centre of our Solar System?

options.rationale: Correct: the Sun is a star and sits at the centre of the Solar System.
The Moon is a natural satellite of Earth, not a star.
Mars is a planet, not a star.
Earth is a planet that orbits the Sun.

items.explanation: Correct: the Sun is a star and sits at the centre of the Solar System.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Why does the same place on Earth have day and then night? (Select ONE)

options.text: The Earth spins on its axis, turning places toward and away from the Sun
options.rationale: Correct: Earth's rotation causes day and night.

options.text: The Sun turns off at night
options.rationale: The Sun keeps shining; the Earth turns away.

options.text: The Moon covers the Sun every night
options.rationale: That is not what causes night.

options.text: Clouds hide the Sun each evening
options.rationale: Clouds are not the cause of night.

items.explanation: Correct: Earth's rotation causes day and night.

items.stem: Select TWO statements that are true about the Moon. (Select TWO)

options.text: It reflects light from the Sun
options.rationale: Correct: the Moon shines by reflecting sunlight.

options.text: It appears to change shape through its phases
options.rationale: Correct: we see phases as the lit part we can see changes.
The Moon is not a star; it makes no light of its own.

options.text: It is larger than the Sun
options.rationale: The Sun is vastly larger than the Moon.

items.explanation: Correct: the Moon shines by reflecting sunlight.
